removability.rationale: The feature has no nav link and one route, but it is not self-contained: removal means edits to the router, the details page module, the Pokémon page, and leaves one dead CSS rule. All edits are obvious, so mid-scale.

evidence: app/src/components.tsx:62 — every card list renders through PokemonCard, so a sprite fix in one component covers home, move, ability and type pages
app/src/api.ts:172 — spriteUrl is the single sprite-URL construction point
app/src/index.tsx:55 — English name fallback re-inlined (also 73, 79, 88) with a different fallback than englishName at app/src/api.ts:160
app/src/api.ts:245 — types derived from type.pokemon scans here, but from pokemon.types at app/src/pages/pokemon.tsx:83
changeability.rationale: Most fixes land in one obvious place (cards, sprite URL, cache, query parsing), but the English-name title fallback is duplicated four times with an inconsistent fallback, and a Pokémon's types are computed from two different API sources.

evidence: app/src/pages/home.tsx:87 — Results component shared between full page and htmx partial; clean partial/full seam
app/src/pages/pokemon.tsx:159 — MovesBody is likewise a standalone swap target
app/public/app.js:2 — client code touches only the data-sort/sortable contract, no server internals
app/src/components.tsx:2 — components import spriteUrl/dexNumber from the data module; mild data/presentation coupling
coupling.rationale: Server and client are clearly separated via a narrow data-attribute contract, routing lives only in index.tsx, and shared state (the cache) is explicit and module-scoped. Only nit: presentation helpers (spriteUrl, dexNumber) are exported from the data layer.

evidence: app/src/api.ts:225 — speciesForPokemon's generic extra parameter absorbs the real variation between card lists without flags
app/src/pages/home.tsx:24 — parseHomeQuery/homeUrl keep URL filter state in one place
app/src/pages/pokemon.tsx:249 — MoveTable column headers and cells at pokemon.tsx:266 are two parallel lists to keep in sync, plus a withLevel flag
app/src/pages/details.tsx:16 — englishShortEffect lives in details.tsx while its sibling text helpers (latestEnglishFlavor) live in api.ts
abstraction_design.rationale: The shared abstractions (Section, CardList, Count, dash, speciesForPokemon, homeUrl) are small, real, and stretch to new cases; an Items page would reuse most of the Moves machinery. Docked for the duplicated MoveTable column definitions and one helper filed in the wrong module.

findings.issue: English display-name resolution is inlined four times (lines 55, 73, 79, 88) with a raw-name fallback that differs from the existing englishName helper's humanized fallback (app/src/api.ts:160), so page title and h1 can drift.
findings.suggestion: Use englishName() in the routers, or compute the title inside each page component next to its h1.

findings.issue: A Pokémon's types are derived from two unrelated API sources: getDex scans type.pokemon lists, while the Pokémon page uses pokemon.types (app/src/pages/pokemon.tsx:83). A bug or API change must be checked in both places.
findings.suggestion: Give the home-page DexEntry its types through the same source (or a single helper) used by the Pokémon page, or add a comment documenting the two paths.

findings.issue: MoveTable's thead column list (lines 249-261) and tbody cell list (lines 266-277) are parallel hand-maintained lists plus a withLevel flag; adding or reordering a column needs two synchronized edits.
findings.suggestion: Define columns once as data (key, label, sort type, render) and generate both header and cells from it.

findings.issue: The /pokemon/:name moves URL with ?game= is constructed three times (index.tsx:65, 66 and the form action at pokemon.tsx:193), each with its own encoding logic.
findings.suggestion: Extract a movesUrl(speciesName, game, {hash}) helper next to homeUrl in pages/pokemon.tsx or home.tsx.

findings.issue: englishShortEffect is module-private to details.tsx while its sibling text helpers (latestEnglishFlavor, cleanText) live in api.ts, splitting the text-normalization helpers across two modules.
findings.suggestion: Move englishShortEffect into api.ts alongside latestEnglishFlavor.

findings.issue: spriteUrl and dexNumber are presentation concerns exported from the data module, so components.tsx:2 depends on data-layer internals for markup.
findings.suggestion: Keep them, but note they're presentation helpers; or move spriteUrl's pattern into components.tsx if the data module should stay transport-only.

findings.issue: The CardList extra callback ignores its p argument and re-indexes data.items[i] by position, a fragile coupling to CardList's iteration order.
findings.suggestion: Use the callback's own item (pass the entry's types through CardData or capture the entry directly).

findings.issue: The no-evolution-chain fallback fabricates a fake ChainLink with url: '', a lie about the API shape that the component must remember not to dereference.
findings.suggestion: Handle the empty-chain case in EvolutionTree (or pass species links, not chain links).

findings.issue: The client sort contract (table.sortable, .sort-button, data-sort, data-sort-type) is implicit stringly-typed coupling with the markup at pokemon.tsx:238-277; renaming an attribute silently breaks sorting.
findings.suggestion: Name the contract: a short comment block in both files, or generate the table's data attributes from one shared constant file.

findings.issue: .card__note is used only by the ability page; deleting the Abilities pages leaves a dead rule with no automated way to notice.
findings.suggestion: Co-locate feature-specific CSS (or accept the small dead-code risk on removal).

summary: A small, cleanly layered codebase where the important seams are real: every htmx partial is a shared component, every card list flows through one PokemonCard, and all API/cache knowledge is confined to api.ts. Editability tax is mostly scattered duplication: English-name titles inlined four times in the router, two sources for a Pokémon's types, and MoveTable's parallel header/cell lists. I'd approve it after the medium findings are addressed.
